title: Show how many invoices are listed next to the Invoices heading
body:
The heading should read like "Invoices (12)", counting the rows currently shown (after any status filter).

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

spec.plan:
Today `/invoices` renders a plain `

Invoices

` above a table of all five seeded invoices, and nothing on the page says how many rows are listed. After the change the heading reads `Invoices (5)`: the number of rows the table actually renders, derived from the same `invoices` array that `` maps over, so the heading and the table cannot disagree. The repo has no status filter today (grep for `status` finds only the invoice field, the `exportableInvoices` sent/paid rule and HTTP status codes), so the request's "after any status filter" is honoured by taking the count from the rendered array rather than from `listInvoices()` or `exportableInvoices()` -- if a filter is added later the heading follows it with no further change, and nothing in this work item adds one (filtering by status is its own open issue, #27; this change is written so it needs no follow-up when that lands). Two constraints the builder must respect: the count has to be interpolated in a single template literal (`{`Invoices (${invoices.length})`}`), not as adjacent JSX children, because React 19's server renderer otherwise emits `Invoices (5)` into the HTML -- the same reason the existing `Total sent:` line is written that way; and no new `lib/` function is warranted, since `invoices.length` is the whole computation and fundamentals.md asks for one domain module, not a second near-duplicate. The `ExportButton` count stays on `exportableInvoices` (3) and is not touched: the heading counts rows shown, the button counts rows exported, and those are deliberately different numbers.
acceptance_checks: Load http://localhost:3000/invoices in a browser: the page's first heading reads exactly `Invoices (5)` instead of `Invoices`.
Count the body rows of the table under that heading: there are 5 (INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003, INV-1004, INV-1005), which is the number shown in the heading.

Fetch the page's HTML directly (`curl -s http://localhost:3000/invoices | grep -F 'Invoices (5)'`): the literal string `Invoices (5)` is present, with no `<!-- -->` markers between `Invoices (`, `5` and `)`.

On the same page, the export button still reads `Export 3 invoices as CSV` -- the heading's 5 counts the rows listed, not the 3 that are exportable, and clicking the button still downloads a CSV of 3 invoices.
tests_added: app/invoices/page.test.tsx: "shows how many invoices are listed, so a reader does not have to count the rows" -- renders `InvoicesPage` and asserts the `<h1>` text is exactly `Invoices (5)` and that the number in it equals the count of `<tbody> <tr>` elements rendered.

app/invoices/page.test.tsx: "counts the rows on the page, not the exportable ones, so the heading cannot read (3) while five rows are visible" -- asserts the heading is not `Invoices (3)` while the export button still reads `Export 3 invoices as CSV`.

research.claim:
The heading to change is a bare `

Invoices

`, and the number of rows shown is `invoices.length` (5), which is not the number already on the page. `app/invoices/page.tsx:11` is a bare `

Invoices

`, and `app/invoices/page.tsx:23` maps over `invoices` (= `listInvoices()`, all five seeded rows) for the table body, while `app/invoices/page.tsx:12` passes `exportable.length` (3) to `ExportButton`. So "rows currently shown" is `invoices.length`, a different number from the one already on the page.

There is no status filter in the app today, so the count must come from the array the table maps over rather than from a filter that does not exist. `grep -rn status app components lib` returns only the `Invoice.status` field, the sent/paid rule inside `exportableInvoices`, the CSV header column and HTTP `res.status` values. There is no filter control, no searchParams read and no client state on the page, and the feature map lists the page as a server component that "lists every invoice in a table". Deriving the count from the array the table maps over satisfies "after any status filter" today and keeps following it if one is added later; building a filter is out of scope for this request.

The count must be interpolated in one template literal, not rendered as an adjacent JSX child, or the server-rendered HTML carries comment markers. Rendering `

Invoices ({n})

` through React 19.3.1's `renderToString` produces `

Invoices (5)

`; a single template literal produces `

Invoices (5)

`. The repo already hit this -- the comment at `app/invoices/page.tsx:33-34` says the `Total sent:` line is one template literal "not adjacent children" for exactly this reason. The builder must follow that pattern, and acceptance check 3 is what catches it if they do not.

research.claim: No new `lib/` function should be added for the count. fundamentals.md's Taste section says to prefer widening an existing pure function over adding a second one that does nearly the same thing, and that there is one domain module which should stay one until a genuinely separate concept appears. `invoices.length` on an array the page already holds is not a domain concept; `totalCents` exists because summing cents is a rule, counting an array is not.

The new cases belong in the existing `app/invoices/page.test.tsx`, which makes it a declared `tests_changed` edit. Tests are colocated as `<name>.test.tsx` beside the source, with `describe` naming the unit and `it` naming the user-visible consequence in a full sentence; component assertions use plain DOM properties rather than jest-dom matchers to keep the dependency list short. `app/invoices/page.test.tsx` already exists with two cases rendering `InvoicesPage` and asserting on `document.body.textContent`, so the new cases belong in that file -- which makes it an edit to an existing test file and therefore a required `tests_changed` entry under policy.yaml's `tests.declared_edits: required`.

The sandbox can exercise all four acceptance checks, and the coverage gate's 80% diff-coverage floor is already met for this file. The manifest's tier is `renders`: the production server starts, `/invoices` answers 200 server-rendered (so a browser screenshot and a `curl` of the HTML both show the real heading), and Chromium can click the export button and capture the download. The coverage gate wants 80% diff coverage per changed file; `npm test -- --coverage` on the tree as it stands reports `app/invoices/page.tsx` at 100% lines, so adding to its existing test file keeps it there.
